beats: Hook: a black box is either all zeros or exactly half ones; for 50-bit inputs a classical check that must be certain may need 2^49 + 1 = 562,949,953,421,313 questions; a quantum computer asks once (line_qc_onequery_drawer_hunt). Cast for QC07-05 and QC07-06 (her lecture Q25-09): the sleuth (short; round wide-brimmed hat, belted raincoat, magnifying glass on a cord), who has to find out, and the host (tall, thin; one big curl of hair, wide lapels, polka-dot bow tie), who keeps the box; the cast is set by line_qc_onequery_two_cabinets, so make it first.

The promise (Q25-09 19:07-21:06): the function is constant (every drawer the same) or balanced (exactly half and half), and we do not know which: line_qc_onequery_two_cabinets. The box is the phase oracle of QC07-03 (reuse line_qc_kickback_sign_box).

Classically (21:06-23:49): if you are lucky, the first answer is a 1 and it must be balanced; in the worst case 2^(n-1) zeros in a row still prove nothing and you need one more: line_qc_onequery_drawer_hunt; reuse line_clerk_ladder or line_card_catalog for more of the drawer wall.

The circuit (23:57-31:20): H on every qubit, the phase oracle, H again, measure; the amplitude of |0...0> is 2^-n sum_x (-1)^f(x): plus or minus 1 when f is constant, exactly 0 when balanced (code letters it; tape Q25-09 s28). Clip 31:20-31:44, "not that complicated once you understand the pattern".

Why it works (31:44-33:16; clip 32:28-33:16, two different interference patterns): when f is constant every path arrives in step at the all-zeros outcome; when it is balanced half arrive flipped and they cancel exactly there (line_qc_onequery_centre_spot; reuse line_qc_interfere_tug_ropes from QC07-04).

Bernstein-Vazirani (33:16-46:39): f(x) = x.v, a panel whose lamp shows the parity of the secretly wired switches you turn on (line_qc_onequery_switch_wiring; it links to the stairwell switches of QC05-06, line_qc_build_stair_switches). Classically you test one switch at a time, n questions (she implies more: correct it, check in FACTS.md); the same circuit returns v in one query, because every wrong v cancels (her words 46:22-46:48). Tape Q25-09 s37.

Honest limits (47:08-48:54; clip 48:02-48:54, "examples we are making up"): a classical checker allowed a tiny chance of error opens a few random drawers and is almost sure (line_qc_onequery_random_drawers; bounded-error classical algorithms solve Deutsch-Jozsa with O(1) queries: say it on screen). Toy problems are test models that showed the way (line_qc_onequery_model_bridge); the next part follows it to a real pattern (QC07-06).
Papers by name only as FACTS.md has them: Deutsch & Jozsa 1992; Bernstein & Vazirani 1993/1997.
Cover (line_qc_cover_07_05; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): the sleuth stands before a towering cabinet of drawers and holds up one finger; the host raises his eyebrows.
